history.summary: NOT A CONVENTIONAL TEMPLE — this is a Ramakrishna Mission ashram/branch centre at Sohra (Cherrapunji/Cherrapunjee), East Khasi Hills, primarily an educational and social-service institution with a shrine. Swami Prabhananda's 1924 visit led to educational work; the official branch centre dates to 1931. It runs dozens of schools (about 77 schools serving roughly 10,000 tribal children, per a 2022 college report), a 30-bed hospital, two mobile medical units, a computer training centre, weaving/tailoring schools, two museums of north-eastern tribal culture, and has sub-centres at Shella (1924) and Sohbarpunjee (1928). Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru donated funds and laid the foundation stone of the central administrative office building in 1952. The Mission's college at Nongthymmai, Mawsmai (Sohra) — inaugurated by CM Conrad Sangma — is the first Ramakrishna Mission college in Northeast India. name: Ramakrishna Mission Sohra
town_description: Sohra (Cherrapunji/Cherrapunjee) is the famous plateau town in Meghalaya's East Khasi Hills, long known for record monsoon rainfall, living root bridges, Nohkalikai Falls, and limestone caves. The Ramakrishna Mission ashram is a well-known educational landmark of the town.
